sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
Tricep Dips on Bench is a bodyweight exercise that targets the triceps using a stable bench for support.

By lowering and pressing your body up with your arms, you build strength and definition in the back of the upper arms.

This movement also engages the shoulders and chest, making it an effective accessory exercise for upper-body pushing strength.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Directly targets the triceps brachii
- Requires no specialized equipment beyond a bench
- Builds upper-body pushing strength
- Easily scaled by bending the knees or extending the legs
- Reinforces shoulder stability and core control
- Great accessory movement for bench press and overhead pressing
- Portable and convenient for at-home or gym training

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps Brachii

Secondary: Anterior Deltoids, Pectoralis Major, Core, Forearms

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Position yourself in front of a sturdy bench, facing away from it.
2. Place your hands on the edge of the bench, fingers pointing towards your body.
3. Extend your legs out in front of you with your heels on the ground.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Slide your buttocks off the bench with your arms fully extended.
2. Support your body weight with your hands gripping the edge.
3. Keep your shoulders packed and chest lifted.

sections.heading: Lower
sections.content:
1. Slowly bend your elbows to lower your body toward the floor.
2. Lower until your elbows reach about a 90-degree angle.
3. Keep your back close to the bench and elbows tracking straight back.

sections.heading: Press and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Push back up by extending your elbows.
2. Focus on using your triceps to drive the movement.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Flaring the elbows out to the sides
- Letting the shoulders shrug up toward the ears
- Drifting too far away from the bench
- Using leg drive instead of the triceps
- Going too low and stressing the shoulders
- Locking out the elbows aggressively at the top
- Allowing the hips to sag during the rep

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Sturdy flat bench, box, or stable elevated surface
- Athletic shoes for secure footing
- Optional: Mat under your feet for grip
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Bench Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Use a bench that will not slide or tip during the movement.
2. Sit on the edge with your hands gripping beside your hips.
3. Fingers should point forward toward your body for wrist comfort.
4. Confirm both hands are evenly placed before starting.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Legs extended forward, heels on floor (bend knees for easier variation).
2. Torso: Tall, ribs down, core braced.
3. Arms: Elbows tracking straight back, not flared.
4. Shoulders: Packed and down, away from the ears.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Parallel Bar Dips: Heavier bodyweight variation
- Tricep Pushdown: Cable-based isolation
- Tricep Skull Crusher: Lying tricep extension
- Close-Grip Bench Press: Compound triceps press
- Diamond Push-Up: Bodyweight triceps emphasis
- Overhead Tricep Extension: Long-head focused isolation

sections.heading: Tricep Dips On Bench Variations
sections.content:
Bent-Knee Bench Dip: Easier variation with feet flat
Straight-Leg Bench Dip: Standard variation as described
Elevated-Foot Bench Dip: Feet on a second bench for greater load
Weighted Bench Dip: Place a plate on the lap for added resistance
Tempo Bench Dip: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy
Pause Bench Dip: Pause at the bottom for greater triceps tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Shoulder Pain: Reduce range of motion and avoid going too low
Wrist Pain: Use parallettes or dip handles for a neutral grip
Elbow Pain: Lighten the load by bending the knees
Low Strength: Start with bent knees and feet flat on the floor
Advanced: Elevate feet or add weight to the lap
Beginners: Use a higher bench and bent knees to learn the pattern
